# libdiginet / fuzz_transport

libdiginet's own fuzz target `fuzz_transport` ([source](source/fuzz_transport.c), modified; see below), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over libdiginet 0.1.1 (FreeMixer/libdiginet at 835f336c).

Runs the library's control-surface session state machine with the harness as its network io and clock. A config is read from the input, then up to 1024 operations: raw or built desk frames, announces, time passing, submitted commands, wake, close, a failing send, and polls. The harness runs its own model of the documented session alongside and holds every frame sent, every notice, the state, the timers and the command queue to that model. Inputs of 64 MiB or more are ignored.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Changed by OSS Verify in one file, fuzz/fuzz_transport.c (in source/ as built): io_recv() runs the harness's model on each frame it hands to the session, just before the session reads it, and the poll's tick alone on an empty frame; receive() no longer runs the model before diginet_session_poll(). No library code changes.
- Why: when the input has poll's recv hand over the same frame twice, the model judged the second copy against the frame in flight before the poll. When that copy is the desk's acknowledgement of a command the poll's tick sent, the session's acked notice is right, and the harness aborted on it.
- Linked against libdiginet at commit 835f336c: the frame, command cursor, controls and decoder sources and the session state machine, built into one static library. The packet socket and descriptor io are not built; the library's own libFuzzer build uses the same sources.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- The session accepts every configuration the harness builds, each within the documented ranges ([lines 1160-1167](source/fuzz_transport.c#L1160-L1167)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Every frame the session sends is a well-formed frame from this host to the known desk, zero-padded to 60 bytes, with the right header sum, and never holds the system family F0 13 xx 70 ([lines 398-420](source/fuzz_transport.c#L398-L420)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Each acknowledgement the session sends echoes the send counter of the desk frame it answers, with no body and retry 0 ([lines 422-430](source/fuzz_transport.c#L422-L430)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A new data frame goes only while online, with nothing in flight and no back-off holding; a retransmission is the frame in flight again, byte for byte but its retry field, which counts 1, 2, ... never past the retry limit, and goes no sooner than the timeout; the acked notice names the frame in flight; the ack-lost notice comes for it after exactly the retry limit ([lines 432-495](source/fuzz_transport.c#L432-L495)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Online only after the desk acknowledges the wake frame and an e1 names this host since then; no wake frame while the desk is in a session with another host, and a wake returns the documented code; each desk announce notice carries the place of this host address, the desk type, the version and the name, and each desk data notice its body, counter and retry ([lines 497-569](source/fuzz_transport.c#L497-L569)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A keepalive goes only when due on its own clock, while online, with nothing in flight and no back-off holding: never early ([lines 571-580](source/fuzz_transport.c#L571-L580)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Each sent data frame stays within the command and body limits and carries the host counter advanced by its commands; with tagged commands, its count is right, it carries only commands submitted and still pending, and a frame with display writes follows the last by at least the configured gap ([lines 582-654](source/fuzz_transport.c#L582-L654)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Submit refuses a command holding F0 13 xx 70 and nothing else as such, and refuses for a full queue only when 512 commands are pending ([lines 656-676](source/fuzz_transport.c#L656-L676)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- After each operation, the session has acknowledged each desk data frame owed an acknowledgement once each time it came, and no other frame ([lines 680-688](source/fuzz_transport.c#L680-L688)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- After each operation, a wake frame went exactly when the host woke and a close frame exactly when owed; each desk data frame but a keepalive or a repeat, each announce and each foreign session was noticed as owed; and the state changed exactly as the header diagram says, in order, each change naming its reason ([lines 690-742](source/fuzz_transport.c#L690-L742)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- After each operation, an acknowledgement of the frame in flight was taken and noticed, a frame in flight still unacknowledged after the timeout was sent again or dropped, and the reported deadline is from now to one second away and never later than the next retransmission ([lines 744-771](source/fuzz_transport.c#L744-L771)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- After each operation, with tagged commands, a keepalive due while online with nothing in flight and no back-off holding has gone: never skipped ([lines 773-783](source/fuzz_transport.c#L773-L783)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- With tagged commands, after each operation the queue holds exactly the pending commands in order, a newer command in its key place, and after a tick a command that may go has gone ([lines 785-819](source/fuzz_transport.c#L785-L819)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libdiginet` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzz_transport.plain` | 64,568 | `bb20ce415827592a9ab28fd0bd5b242215eb3ff03b629e12a4723cc6f44ace56` |
| ubsan | `fuzz_transport.ubsan` | 67,496 | `af7b86991906e2fd59d929595aaaf239f5f5805109f480ef9ef99e286a97840d` |
| asan | `fuzz_transport.asan` | 616,792 | `e89be137db17b720e0310addc2dcc601998945478a9102e6a9850b0566106350` |
| asan-ubsan | `fuzz_transport.asan-ubsan` | 615,864 | `41113a03c82fde8282db830ab5f4fbe376e392a38d22670b8cb8c9f02969ece4` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
